newsitem.title: USA: Clinton would mull law aiding retirees if re-elected.
newsitem.headline: Clinton would mull law aiding retirees if re-elected.

text.p: If President Clinton wins re-election his administration will consider legislation to help retirees at risk of losing health insurance from their prior employers, Labour Secretary Robert Reich said Monday.
Reich did not specify what legislation could be drafted and said the administration wanted to help retirees without discouraging companies from offering health insurance.
But he told reporters the possibilities ran the gamut from laws requiring more accurate disclosure to retirees to better ensuring that contracts promising long-term benefits are enforced.
U.S. law does not require employers to insure workers or retirees and increasing numbers of businesses have dropped the costly benefit.
In 1988 37 percent of retirees had insurance, which dropped to 27 percent by 1994, according to Labour Department statistics. Medicare does not cover people under age 65 even if they are retired.

Reich said he was concerned by workers who retired, or took early retirement packages, believing they had life-long coverage only to find out later that a small print "reserve clause" gave the former employer a legal right to renege.
"The retirees can be left holding the bag," he said. "We don't think it's fair that employees should be surprised."
The Labour Department has filed friend-of-the-court briefs in several cases involving retirees who lost benefits, including cases at General Motors and Pabst Brewing Co.
The department Monday also issued a four-page bulletin for retirees or people preparing to retire on how to inform themselves of what benefits are due to them.
